A tighter ADX threshold and a reduced supertrend multiplier capture more trend‑driven moves while still filtering out weak trends; the ATR‑based exit ensures volatility‑adjusted risk control, improving trade frequency without sacrificing risk‑reward balance.

Using the supertrend as a trend filter combined with a strong ADX (>35) ensures entries are only taken when a clear trend exists, while exiting on a direction change or weak ADX (<15) limits exposure to reversals. ATR-based SL/TP adapts risk to current volatility, improving risk‑reward balance.

Combining the supertrend trend signal with a longer‑term EMA filter aligns entries with the prevailing market direction, reducing whipsaw trades during low‑volatility periods and thus lowering drawdown, while the ATR‑based stop and TP maintain disciplined risk management.

Entering only when price is above the supertrend upper band (or below the lower band) while ADX confirms a strong trend (>30) reduces false signals in choppy markets; exiting on a supertrend direction change or ADX weakening protects from lingering in losing trades, improving risk‑adjusted returns.

Using the supertrend to confirm trend direction combined with a high ADX filter reduces false entries in choppy markets, while ATR-based stop and take‑profit levels automatically adjust to prevailing volatility, improving risk‑reward balance.
Combining the supertrend trend signal with a strong ADX filter and an EMA confirmation reduces whipsaw entries and captures genuine trend moves, while ATR‑based risk controls adapt to volatility.
